subject.title: [Bug]:  Isolated cron session agent loop continues consuming tokens after run marked "ok"

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: The linked fix and the competing open PR encode opposite product contracts, and choosing between automatic cleanup, upgrade migration, or rejection affects existing scheduled jobs and session-state retention.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep the linked PR direction, but require a path for existing omitted persisted jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Choose the competing strict-validation direction and rework or close the linked defaulting PR after documenting user recovery.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land the default only for newly created jobs and document that existing implicit jobs need operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep the linked PR direction, but require a path for existing omitted persisted jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans cron store migration/default semantics and product compatibility, and steipete has recent history in that store boundary.
